Build PHASE 1 of "Sitewave" — a productized web-design agency — as an add-on module inside the Nxeon platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres at /opt/nxeon). It's a placeholder brand: name "Sitewave", palette indigo #4F46E5 + coral #FB7185 + ink #0B1020, tagline "Websites that win you customers.", placeholder domain agency.revsports.ca (store as config, don't rely on DNS).

READ FIRST: the architecture + board for this project:
- /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/agency/architecture.md
- /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/agency/board.json (implement the "Phase 1" column).
Study Nxeon conventions: lib/admin-groups.ts (ADMIN_NAV — you'll add a new top-level section), lib/rbac.ts (HREF_AREA + requireArea, map new routes to area "platform"), components/ui/primitives.tsx (reuse PageHeader/StatCard/Badge/EmptyState), an existing admin page + its lib/actions-*.ts pattern, components/portal/Shell.tsx icons map (use an existing key like "globe" or "sparkle"), and lib/anthropic.ts (askClaude — the platform ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; degrade gracefully if unset, like lib/marketing/draft-gen.ts does).

=== HARD GUARDRAILS ===
- Branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase1` off main (main is at a4c1f3f). Commit + `git push -u origin feature/agency-sitewave-phase1`. Do NOT commit to main, do NOT deploy, do NOT `prisma db push` any DB, do NOT edit .env.
- NO real scraping of live business websites. NO outreach sending. NO live subdomain provisioning this phase (deploy-to-subdomain is a QUEUED/stubbed action only).
- `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` MUST pass with 0 errors; add tests where sensible and keep them passing.

=== PHASE 1 DELIVERABLES ===
1) Prisma schema (additive, prefix models to avoid collisions, e.g. Agency*): AgencyVertical (slug, name, description), AgencyTemplate (verticalId, name, a JSON structure/section-schema), AgencyProspect (businessName, vertical, contactEmail?, currentSiteUrl?, notes, status enum PROSPECT/GENERATED/SENT/WON/LOST), AgencyDemoSite (prospectId, templateId, siteIR Json, renderedHtml, slug for the would-be subdomain, status enum DRAFT/GENERATED/DEPLOYED_STUB, noindex bool default true, createdAt), and a generation log. Index appropriately.
2) A starter per-vertical template library (seed 4-5 verticals: dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon), each with a section schema (hero, services, about, testimonials, contact).
3) The spec-site GENERATOR core (lib/agency/generate.ts, pure where possible): given a prospect (businessName, vertical, optional pasted existing-site text — NOT scraped), call askClaude to produce a structured "Site IR" (JSON: hero copy, services, about, CTA, palette suggestion) constrained to the vertical's section schema; then a DETERMINISTIC renderer (lib/agency/render.ts) that turns Site IR → a self-contained static HTML page. LEGAL GUARDRAILS baked into the renderer (per the architecture's biggest risk): business NAME in plain type only (no re-hosted logo), an "inspired-by"/neutral palette (not the business's exact brand), a visible "Independent concept — not affiliated with {business}" disclaimer, and <meta name="robots" content="noindex">. Degrade to a deterministic template fill if no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
4) Admin UI under a NEW top-level nav section "Agency" (Sitewave): 
   - /admin/agency — Overview (counts: prospects, demos generated, by status).
   - /admin/agency/verticals — manage verticals + templates.
   - /admin/agency/prospects — CRUD prospects (manual add + CSV paste); from a prospect, "Generate demo".
   - /admin/agency/demos — list generated demo sites; PREVIEW the rendered HTML (in an iframe/newtab via a serve route app/api/agency/demo/[id]/preview that returns the stored HTML with noindex headers); a "Deploy to subdomain" button that is a STUB (marks DEPLOYED_STUB + records the intended slug.agency.revsports.ca; real provisioning is Phase 2, documented).
   - Integration hook: a "Send to outreach" action that creates/links a Cold Email Engine Business+Contact from the prospect (reuse the coldemail models/actions) — but does NOT send.
   Server actions in lib/actions-agency.ts (each re-checks requireArea("platform")). Match existing admin look; sentence case.
5) Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md with a "Sitewave (Marketing Agency) — Phase 1" section.

When done: prisma generate + npm run build clean; commit + push the branch; report files added/changed, models added, build/test result, and the staging command `cd /opt/nxeon && bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/agency-sitewave-phase1`. Do not deploy.

1	# Marketing Agency — Architecture & Build Plan
2	
3	**Author:** Research/architecture agent · **Date:** 2026-08-10
4	**Status:** Research + planning only. No code written, nothing deployed, no APIs mutated.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Product Overview
9	
10	A **productized web-design agency as software**. Two halves:
11	
12	1. **Demo-Gen Engine (flagship, the wedge):** Pick a business vertical (dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon, HVAC, med-spa, auto shop…) → load a vertical-specific site template → take a target business from a prospect list → scrape/read its *current* website → extract brand (logo, colors, copy, services, hours, reviews) → generate a demonstrably *better* AI-built site → deploy it to a per-prospect subdomain (`joes-diner.demos.agency-domain.com`) → hand the link to the **Cold Email Engine** (separate product) for outreach: *"We built you a free redesign — here it is."* When they click, a **claim/CTA flow** captures the warm lead.
13	2. **Agency CRM / Pipeline:** Once a prospect replies, the demo becomes a deal. Pipeline (Lead → Demo Sent → Opened → Replied → Call → Won → Onboarding → Live → Retainer), proposals/contracts, billing, and handoff (promote the demo to a real, owned site).
14	
15	It ships **standalone** (`agency.<domain>`) *and* as a **Nxeon admin add-on module** (`/admin/agency`), because Nxeon is the central hub and already owns the hosting infra the demos deploy onto.
16	
17	### Core value chain
18	`Vertical + Template Library` × `AI Generation` × `Cheap per-prospect Deploy` × `Personalized Outreach` = high-conversion lead-gen. The moat is **volume + personalization + the demo already exists** — the prospect sees the finished product, not a pitch.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 2. Competitors & Positioning
23	
24	| Product | What it is | Price | Relevance |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| **Durable** | GPT-driven 30-sec site builder for local service businesses | ~$12–15/mo | Closest to our *generation* quality bar; all-in-one but generic templates. |
27	| **B12** | AI site in ~60s + human-assisted service tier | $42–$399/mo | Hybrid AI+expert; our "won client" tier competes here. |
28	| **10Web** | AI → full WordPress + managed hosting, Elementor editor | $10–20/mo+ | Proves AI→editable→hosted pipeline; WP lock-in. |
29	| **Framer AI / v0 (Vercel)** | AI generates high-design React/Framer sites | v0 $20/mo (5k credits); Framer usage-based | Best-in-class *output quality*; not an agency/outreach engine. |
30	| **Readdy / LeadGen.ai / ManyRequests-style "spec site" plays** | Auto-generate a personalized demo per lead + link it in outreach | agency SaaS pricing | **Direct competitor to our exact play** — validates the model. |
31	
32	**Positioning:** We are *not* selling a DIY builder. We sell **done-for-you demos at scale that convert cold prospects**, backed by a real agency pipeline + Nxeon hosting. Differentiators: (a) **per-vertical designed template library** (not generic), (b) **real brand extraction** from the prospect's existing site so the demo feels bespoke, (c) **owned hosting** = near-zero marginal deploy cost, (d) integrated CRM→billing→handoff, (e) tight loop with the Cold Email Engine.
33	
34	Sources: NxCode AI-builder roundup, fahimai 10Web-vs-B12, G2/B12 pricing, v0/Framer reviews, Readdy/LeadGen.ai agency pages (see §12).
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 3. External APIs / Credentials Required
39	
40	| Need | Recommended | Pricing note | Link |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| **LLM generation** (copy, section selection, structured layout JSON) | **Anthropic Claude** — Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15 per MTok) for most, Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5) for extraction/classification, Opus 4.8 ($5/$25) only for hero/design decisions | A full site gen ≈ 30–120k tokens ⇒ **~$0.10–$0.60/site** at Sonnet. Batch API halves it. | anthropic.com/pricing |
43	| **Web scraping / extraction** | **Firecrawl** (`/scrape` + `/extract` structured) | Free 1k credits; Hobby $16/mo 5k; Standard $83/mo 100k. ~1 credit/page (~$0.0008/page on Standard); structured `/extract` billed separately (~$172–188/mo min if heavy). Start Free/Hobby. | firecrawl.dev/pricing |
44	| **Scraping fallback / cheap** | Self-hosted **Playwright** + Cheerio + a color/logo extractor | Free (compute only) — use for MVP to avoid Firecrawl bill; Firecrawl for hard/JS-heavy sites. | playwright.dev |
45	| **Logo / brand assets** | **Brandfetch API** (logo+colors+fonts by domain) or Clearbit-style logo endpoint | Brandfetch has a free dev tier; good instant-brand source, avoids re-hosting their exact logo (see legal §11). | brandfetch.com/developers |
46	| **Business lists / enrichment** | Google Places API (place details, reviews, categories) / existing prospect CSV | Places: pay-per-call, ~$17/1k Details. Often the list comes *from* the Cold Email Engine. | developers.google.com/maps |
47	| **Screenshots** (before/after visual in outreach) | Firecrawl screenshot or self-hosted Playwright | Included/free. | — |
48	| **Stock imagery** for verticals | Unsplash API / Pexels API (free) or generated (SDXL/Flux via Replicate) | Free tiers; generated hero imagery optional. | unsplash.com/developers |
49	| **Deploy / hosting** | **Reuse Nxeon** shared-hosting nodes + wildcard DNS + certbot (see §7). No new vendor. | Marginal ≈ compute only. | internal |
50	| **DNS** | Nxeon already uses **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`); add a wildcard `*.demos.<domain>` A record once. | flat | internal |
51	| **Email sending** | **NOT here** — delegate to the separate **Cold Email Engine** via internal API/webhook. | — | internal |
52	| **Payments/billing** | Reuse Nxeon **Stripe** integration for won-client retainers. | Stripe fees | internal |
53	
54	**Credentials to provision (env):** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `BRANDFETCH_API_KEY` (optional), `GOOGLE_PLACES_KEY` (optional), `UNSPLASH_KEY` (optional), plus reused Nxeon secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, Namecheap, Stripe) when running as add-on. Store per-tenant if multi-tenant.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## 4. Recommended Tech Stack
59	
60	- **Framework:** Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript (matches Nxeon exactly; shares `components/portal/Shell.tsx`, `components/ui/`, `app/globals.css` design system).
61	- **DB:** PostgreSQL + Prisma. Standalone gets its own DB; as add-on, additive tables in the Nxeon schema (prefix `agency_` / `Agency*` models, mirroring how shared-hosting added `HostingNode`/`HostingAccount` without touching the VPS models).
62	- **Generation:** Anthropic SDK with **structured output** (JSON Schema / tool-use) to emit a validated **Site IR** (page → sections → blocks with typed props), *not* raw HTML. Deterministic renderer maps IR → React components from the vertical template. This is the 2026 best practice (structured output over free-form HTML — Outlines/tool-use) and keeps output on-brand and safe.
63	- **Rendering the demo:** Two options — (A) **static export** of the generated site (Next static/HTML) served as a plain vhost on a Nxeon shared node (cheapest, safest, no runtime); (B) a single multi-tenant Next app that renders by subdomain from stored IR. **MVP = (A) static export** (near-zero cost, trivially cacheable, no per-demo process).
64	- **Background work:** a worker/queue mirroring Nxeon's `HostingTask`/worker-tick pattern (jobs: `SCRAPE`, `GENERATE`, `RENDER`, `DEPLOY`, `SCREENSHOT`, `NOTIFY_OUTREACH`). Status-driven state machine so a demo self-completes and retries.
65	- **Storage:** generated assets + screenshots to disk/object store; IR JSON in Postgres.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 5. Data Model Sketch (Prisma-ish)
70	
71	```
72	Vertical           id, slug, name, defaultTemplateId, promptPack (json), heroImagerySet
73	Template           id, verticalId, name, sectionCatalog(json), themeTokens(json), previewImg
74	Prospect           id, businessName, domain, category, vertical, city,
75	                   sourceEmail?, phone?, placesId?, importBatchId, status
76	BrandProfile       id, prospectId, logoUrl, colors(json), fonts(json),
77	                   extractedCopy(json), services(json), hours, reviews(json),
78	                   currentScreenshotUrl, rawScrape(json), extractedAt
79	Demo               id, prospectId, templateId, siteIR(json), status(enum),
80	                   subdomain, deployUrl, screenshotUrl, version,
81	                   generatedAt, deployedAt, expiresAt
82	DemoEvent          id, demoId, type(SENT|OPENED|CLICKED|CLAIMED|REPLIED), meta, at
83	Job                id, kind, refId, status, attempts, error, payload(json)   // worker queue
84	Deal               id, prospectId, demoId, stage(enum), value, owner, notes
85	Proposal           id, dealId, url, amount, status, sentAt, signedAt
86	Client             id, dealId, hostingAccountId?, billingSubId?, liveUrl, handoffAt
87	Setting/Tenant     apiKeys, brandGuardrails, allowlist/denylist, per-tenant config

94	## 6. Generation Pipeline (step by step)
95	
96	1. **Intake.** Prospect added (CSV import, Google Places pull, or handed over by Cold Email Engine). Assign vertical (heuristic on Places category + LLM classifier fallback).
97	2. **Scrape.** Fetch current site: Playwright (MVP) or Firecrawl `/scrape`. Capture HTML, full-page screenshot, and (Firecrawl `/extract` or Brandfetch) structured brand: **logo, palette, fonts, headings, services, hours, address, phone, review snippets**. Respect robots/ToS (§11). Store `BrandProfile`.
98	3. **Normalize + classify.** Cheap Haiku call: confirm vertical, summarize services, pull a value-prop, flag if the current site is missing (a *no-site* prospect is an even better target — generate from Places data only).
99	4. **Plan.** Sonnet call with **structured output** → **Site IR**: choose sections from the vertical template's `sectionCatalog` (hero, services grid, about, testimonials, gallery, booking CTA, map, FAQ, footer), write on-brand copy, map extracted colors→theme tokens (with contrast/accessibility guardrails), pick imagery. Validate IR against JSON Schema; reject/repair invalid.
100	5. **Render.** Deterministic renderer: IR + template React components + theme tokens → **static HTML/CSS** export. No prospect logo re-hosted verbatim if legal flag set — use their name in brand type + a neutral/generated mark (§11). Inject a discreet **"Demo by <Agency> — not affiliated with <Business>"** disclaimer + a **claim CTA**.
101	6. **QA gate.** Automated checks: valid HTML, Lighthouse/perf, no broken links, contrast, no profanity/hallucinated claims, required disclaimer present. Optional human-approve queue before it can be sent.
102	7. **Deploy.** Provision subdomain on Nxeon (§7), publish static files, issue SSL, warm cache. Store `deployUrl`.
103	8. **Screenshot before/after.** Render a side-by-side (their old site vs. our new) for the outreach email.
104	9. **Hand to Cold Email Engine.** Emit `demo.ready` webhook/event with `{prospect, deployUrl, beforeAfterImg, claimUrl}`. Cold Email Engine owns sending. We only track opens/clicks via the claim link + a tracking pixel/redirect we host.
105	10. **Warm-lead capture.** Claim page (`/claim/<token>`) = "Love it? Book a call / make it yours." Fires `DemoEvent` → creates/advances a `Deal`.
106	11. **Lifecycle.** Demos **auto-expire** (e.g. 30 days) and are torn down to reclaim subdomains and reduce brand-exposure risk unless converted.

155	## 10. Key Risks
156	
157	1. **Legal/brand exposure (biggest)** — see §11. Unsolicited use of a business's logo/brand in a live public demo is the single largest risk; mitigations are mandatory, not optional.
158	2. **Email deliverability & spam law** — outreach volume can nuke sending domains and trip CAN-SPAM/GDPR/CASL. Owned by Cold Email Engine, but our demo links/domains share reputation; keep demo domain separate from sending domain, honor opt-out, throttle.
159	3. **Generation quality variance** — a bad demo hurts the brand and the pitch. Mitigate with QA gate + human approve early + structured IR (not free HTML).
160	4. **Cost blow-ups** — Firecrawl `/extract` and Opus can get pricey at volume; default to Playwright + Sonnet/Haiku + Batch; cap per-prospect spend.
161	5. **Hosting abuse/reputation** — many auto-generated sites on shared IPs can look spammy to Google Safe Browsing; use `noindex` on demos, `robots: disallow`, isolate demo IP from production customer IPs.
162	6. **Scraping breakage / anti-bot** — sites block scrapers; Firecrawl fallback + graceful "generate from Places data only."
163	7. **Multi-tenant data isolation** if sold to sub-agencies.

167	## 11. Legal / Ethical / Compliance (MANDATORY)
168	
169	- **Trademark — nominative fair use.** Using a business's **plain-text name** to identify them (in the demo + outreach) is generally defensible nominative fair use: (a) they can't be identified without the name, (b) use only as much as necessary, (c) do nothing implying sponsorship/endorsement. **Using their distinctive logo, exact font, or full color scheme is riskier** — courts treat visual branding as more likely to imply endorsement and as "more than necessary." **Rule:** default to *name in type + a neutral/AI-generated mark + a palette inspired-by (not identical)*; only re-host their actual logo with consent. (INTA, Chase Law, Nolo, Davis+Gilbert.)
170	- **Copyright.** Their site copy/images are their (or a third party's) copyright. Don't republish verbatim; **rewrite** copy (we do — it's a *redesign*) and use **our/licensed/generated imagery**, not scraped photos. Logos may also be copyrighted separately from TM.
171	- **Clear disclaimer on every demo:** *"Unofficial concept redesign created by <Agency>. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or an official site of <Business>."* — kills the endorsement inference.
172	- **noindex / robots disallow** on all demos so they never rank or get mistaken for the real site; auto-expire + teardown when not converted.
173	- **Anti-spam:** outreach must comply with **CAN-SPAM** (US: valid physical address, honor opt-out, no deceptive headers), **GDPR/PECR** (EU/UK: legitimate-interest/consent), **CASL** (Canada: consent). Enforced by Cold Email Engine, but we provide **opt-out/takedown** on the demo + a suppression/deny list honored before any generation.
174	- **Scraping ToS/robots.** Respect `robots.txt` and site ToS; scrape only public pages, low rate, identify a UA; prefer Places/Brandfetch (licensed) over deep scraping. Some jurisdictions/sites prohibit scraping — keep an allow/deny list and a kill switch.
175	- **Takedown SLA + audit log** of what we scraped, generated, deployed, and sent per prospect.

A productized web-design agency shipped as a Nxeon admin add-on module. **"Sitewave" is a placeholder
brand** (name, palette indigo `#4F46E5` + coral `#FB7185` + ink `#0B1020`, tagline "Websites that win you

**not** resolved via DNS). Built on branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase1`.

**The Phase 1 loop.** Add a *prospect* (a target business — manual or CSV, **no scraping**), assign a
*vertical*, then **Generate demo** → the generator writes a structured **Site IR** (JSON: hero copy,
services, about, CTA, an inspired-by palette) constrained to the vertical's section schema, and a
**deterministic renderer** turns the IR into a self-contained static HTML page. **Preview** it in a new tab.
**Deploy to subdomain** is a Phase-1 **stub** (records the intended `slug.agency.revsports.ca` host, marks
the demo `DEPLOYED_STUB` — no nginx/DNS/filesystem write). **Send to outreach** creates/links a Cold Email
`Business` + `Contact` from the prospect (reuses the existing coldemail models) but **sends nothing**.

**Generation (`lib/agency/generate.ts`).** Calls Claude via the platform `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
(`lib/anthropic.ts` `askClaude`, model `claude-opus-4-8`) to emit the Site IR as JSON. **Degrades
gracefully** exactly like `lib/marketing/draft-gen.ts`: with no key (or on any API/JSON error) it falls
back to a deterministic per-vertical template fill, so a demo is **always** produced. All output is coerced
through `coerceSiteIR` (`lib/agency/schema.ts`) which never throws — every field is defaulted, palette hex
validated, service/testimonial counts clamped.

**Legal guardrails baked into the renderer (`lib/agency/render.ts`).** Per architecture §11 (the biggest
risk), every rendered demo — LLM or fallback — carries: the business **name in plain type only** (no
re-hosted logo, ever), an **inspired-by palette** (never the business's exact brand), a visible
**"Independent concept — not affiliated with {business}"** disclaimer in both the top banner and the footer,
and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. All IR-derived text is HTML-escaped; the renderer is
pure + deterministic (no clock, no randomness, no network). It self-asserts the guardrails and
`generateDemo` **refuses to persist** a demo that fails the assertion. The preview route also sends
`X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.

**Schema additions (additive, all `Agency*`-prefixed — never touch VPS/hosting/coldemail models).**
`AgencyVertical` (slug, name, description), `AgencyTemplate` (verticalId, name, JSON `structure` /
section-schema), `AgencyProspect` (businessName, vertical, contactEmail?, currentSiteUrl?, pastedSiteText,
notes, `status` enum `PROSPECT|GENERATED|SENT|WON|LOST`, outreachBusinessId?), `AgencyDemoSite` (prospectId,
templateId?, `siteIR` Json, renderedHtml, slug, `status` enum `DRAFT|GENERATED|DEPLOYED_STUB`, `noindex`
default true, intendedHost?, deployedAt?), and `AgencyGenerationLog` (demoId, mode `llm|fallback`, model,
ok, message). Indexed on slug/status/vertical/createdAt/foreign keys. **Requires a migration before use —
this branch does NOT run `prisma db push`.**

**Starter template library (`lib/agency/templates.ts` + `prisma/seed-agency.ts`).** Five seeded verticals —
dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon — each with a section schema (hero, services, about, testimonials,
contact) and deterministic fallback content. `templates.ts` is the single source of truth shared by the seed
and the generator's fallback, so the DB library and the no-API path stay in lockstep. Seed manually:
`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed-agency.ts`.
